... RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD, AGA FOR R.5)
 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH THE IMPUGNED ORDER DTD.21.12.2013 AS PER ANNEXURE-A AND QUASH THE ENTIRE PROCEEDINGS INITIATED BY R.5 VIDE ANNEXURE - A AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
Bantwal Municipality has issued a trade licence to the petitioner, on 22.01.2013, to run a Chicken Stall.
He has obtained NOC on 21.10.2013 from the Food, Safety and Standard Department to run the business of Chicken Stall.

Respondent Nos.1 to 3 have filed an appeal, before the 5th respondent,
on 18.12.2013, under Sections 343 and 306 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, questioning the trade licence issued in favour of the petitioner.

Respondent No.5 having passed an interim order of stay of the operation of the trade licence issued in favour of the petitioner, this writ petition was filed on 20.02.2014, to quash the interim order dated 21.12.2013 passed by the 5th respondent and to grant the consequential reliefs including the quashing of entire proceedings initiated before respondent No.5 or in the alternative to direct respondent No.5 to decide the appeal expeditiously.
2. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 have preferred an appeal vide Annexure-D before the respondent No.5.
Annexure-A is the notice of the said appeal cum intimation with regard to an interim order passed staying the operation of the impugned license, till 09.01.2014.
In response to Annexure-A, the petitioner has filed statement of objections vide Annexures - F and G before respondent No.5.

The Abdul Karim vs Sandeep Menzes on 24 February, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68980539/
2
interim order passed vide Annexure-A was operative upto 09.01.2014.
The writ petition does not make clear as to whether the said interim order was extended subsequently or otherwise.
In the circumstances, it is unnecessary to quash Annexure-A or the proceedings initiated before the 5th respondent.

However, the 5th respondent is hereby directed to decide the appeal vide Annexure-D, expeditiously and within a period of two months from the date a copy of this order becomes available, after giving reasonable opportunity of hearing to both parties.

It is made clear that no opinion is expressed with regard to the contentions raised against the impugned proceedings by the petitioner and it is for the 5th respondent to decide the appeal, in accordance with law.
